newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - January 27.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - January 27.

text.p: Following are the highlights of stories reported in the Irish press on Monday.

- The first preliminary session this year of the multi-party talks on the future of Northern Ireland will be convened at Stormont on Monday morning in an atmosphere of deepening division and concern over recent IRA and Loyalist paramilitary violence.
- World Bank financial policies in the most impoverished African countries are frustrating the aim of Irish aid to help the "poorest of the poor", according to a leading Africanist.
- For the first time a shortage in donations is forcing the Blood Transfusion Services Board to import blood stocks.
- The Irish government said it has no immediate plans to seek a new inquiry into the events of Bloody Sunday.
- The recent rise in the Irish pound against the mark and other core European currencies has had a devastating impact on many Irish exporters.
- The row over the status of Regional Technical Colleges is rapidly turning into an election headache for the Irish government.
- The standoff between the Irish government, teacher unions and the Catholic Church over new employment equality legislation may be resolved shortly.
- Britain is planning to suspend the interparty talks in Northern Ireland until after the general election and politicians there fear they may never be resumed.
- The Irish Central Bank cannot be seen to be doing nothing in the face of the growing consumer boom, Riada Stockbrokers say in their weekly preview of financial markets.
- If credit unions were allowed to offer unlimited loans and savings, the government would have to abolish their DIRT tax exemption, Commerce Minister Pat Rabbitte said on Sunday.
